gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Warnes draws stretched, spacious letters whose ink strokes taper out before they touch, all in one unvarying line. Noto Sans Hanunoo follows with lowercase that fills most of the line height and terminals left easy and open.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew reads modern and businesslike, with wide gaps between curve ends and stems. Warnes does bold, expressive display work, as if bent from a single length of wire, while the body font handles the steady reading.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-hk: Warnes stretches out wide and bold, one monoline stroke from start to finish. Noto Sans HK keeps its large lowercase forms tight under the ascenders, and its brush ends lift away before each curve closes, so paragraphs read in a compact, tidy texture.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-imperial-aram: Stretched, bold and wiry. Warnes has no stress in any curve, while Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic brings open-pincer c shapes and a short step up to its capitals, so the heading's loud spacing sits comfortably over a friendlier plain sans.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional: Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian reads clean and open, with big eyes on every e and a and a deep middle band. Warnes, flat and unmodulated in its line weight, stretches across the top with expressive spacing, and the plain sans below simply lets it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-jp: Noto Sans JP stands very tall in its x-height, with curves that sweep open instead of curling shut. And Warnes, cut like sign-shop vinyl to a single line width, adds a bold, stretched voice above that plain sans.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Warnes is a monoline skeleton with tapering ink strokes, spread wide and loud across the line. Noto Sans Kaithi settles underneath, its lowercase filling the line like capitals.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Noto Sans Kannada is approachable, with a gentle bump up to capitals. Its sans curves open wide at both ends, which sets off the bold, stretched Warnes, whose rounds and stems all share one weight.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Noto Sans Kayah Li has brush ends lifted away before curves close, and capitals only slightly taller than its lowercase. Noto Sans Kayah Li would swallow a heading shrunk down, because Warnes, with its neon-tube consistency, needs size and spacing to stay expressive.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Expressive and stretched, Warnes looks traced with a marker, tapering before strokes touch. Noto Sans Kharoshthi adds a thick, dark stripe of lowercase with curves that never close back, giving the sans a sturdy, friendly footing under it.
